# CXNM - Standard - WIN - D - Google Chrome Updates

Makes sure a Chrome update takes effect within three days: relaunch notification required, forced relaunch outside working hours, and sooner when the version is badly out of date.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | All Devices |
| Source | Google Chrome policy in the settings catalog (chromeintunev1, chromeintunev141) — values chosen to match the Edge counterpart in this baseline; ids, options and ranges verified against DCv2/Settings in pl4nty/intune-change-tracking |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Google_Chrome_Updates.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Google_Chrome_Updates.json) |

> Google Update itself (update policy, channel) is not in the settings catalog: the `update~policy~cat_google~cat_googleupdate` definitions that do exist belong to the Edge updater, whose ADMX is a fork of Google Update that kept the old category names. As long as nobody turns updates off through Google Update, Chrome updates itself; this policy makes sure those updates actually take effect. RelaunchFastIfOutdated lives in the chromeintunev141 namespace, the rest in chromeintunev1. A device that is off at night only relaunches in the next window.
